purpose: Records the 2026-09-30 fix of the required osv-scanner check, which fails on fresh runs since OSV records five advisories published that day (14:46Z to 15:41Z): GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw and GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g (urllib3 2.7.0, all fixed in 2.8.0) and GHSA-42vr-xj54-vc7v (PyJWT below 2.15.0, fixed in 2.15.0) in the OpenHands recipe lock, and GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j (next 16.3.5, fixed in 16.3.6) in the frozen macOS variant lock. The OpenHands lock is relocked onto urllib3 2.8.0 and PyJWT 2.15.0 with the recipe's own method (only those two entries change). The macOS lock is a frozen evidence artifact for which the tree records no owner; it cannot be patched, so its dated exception lives in a config of its own and security-scan.yml scans that one lock in an invocation of its own under it, every other lock under the ordinary config, which holds no such exception (OSV-Scanner applies an explicit --config to every input of one invocation, so the scanner itself keeps the exception from reaching any other lock). One change carries all of it, because the check scans the whole inventory. The name of this record predates the PyJWT advisory, whose fix joined the change once the workspace's 7-day window opened (section B, 16:56:34Z).
authorization: Started from a peer report that the required check failed on fresh runs (peer messages are not retained evidence; the reproduction in section E is). The lock lane is the OpenHands recipe's. For the frozen macOS lock the tree records no owner (returned outputs, section F: its only commit is #201, its experiment record has no owner, session or author key, docs/lanes.md does not name it). The split scan was asked for by the Codex root after its independent verifier refuted the first design (see independent_review). No user decision is needed: every fix follows the repository's own policy and method.
evidence_class: Local runs on this host of the pinned OSV-Scanner 2.6.0 with the repository's configs and the workflow's own scan step (run by bash from the workflow file), a local reproduction of the relock with uv 0.12.17 from the pinned upstream source archive, the recipe's own install sequence in a scratch venv, reads of git objects, the OSV API and PyPI, and 5 read-only cross-family reviews of the superseded first design (codex exec as typed in relock-2026-09-30-urllib3.cross-family-review.sh.txt; their own output records no model or effort). Static and local; not an execution of the recipe, of any worker or of any application; the CI run on the merged head is the authority for the required check.
limitations: The relock covers only the recipe venv. The agent-server image's server is a PyInstaller build of upstream's unchanged uv.lock (pins.json source_archive), which still pins urllib3 2.7.0 and PyJWT 2.13.0 or older, and the grader venv has its own lock; neither is changed here (the same scope limit as the earlier PyJWT relock record).

The macOS exception is a statement about this repository only: it keeps the variant's package.json and lock (two files, no application source), so it says nothing about the application that ran on the Mac on 2026-09-24. It expires on 2026-12-24 and then needs a renewed dated reason, or the lock leaving the inventory.

The split scan scopes the exception by config: a future exception for another frozen artifact needs its own config, an inventory entry naming it, a FROZEN_LOCKS row and a workflow invocation; the workflow's count check fails an entry that names a config nothing scans.

On events other than pull_request the frozen scan writes its own SARIF report; it is uploaded under its own category (osv-scanner-frozen-macos). Both reports were empty in the local run (section H), and the upload step itself was not run here (it needs a token); its shape is checked by tests/test_workflow_hardening.py.

Section E's main control is the workflow's old single invocation over origin/main's 49 entries; section H runs the new workflow step, extracted from the file, with the pinned binary. The CI run on the merged head is the authority for the required check. The failing set is whatever OSV lists at the time of a scan (each scan carries its time), and more advisories can land before a merge.

A separately drafted OpenHands 1.50 Linux lock (draft PR 535, head 00aa6c25fe6f27e9f5974e9f6a5592aa31683479 as fetched, sha256 383ccc5b87702174e471732872f002f1621186710402d048acc2b1910306e106) carries urllib3 2.7.0 and pyjwt 2.14.0 too (section G); this change does not touch its files.

split_scan.why: OSV-Scanner 2.6.0 applies an explicit --config to every input of one invocation (docs/configuration.md; internal/config/manager.go, Manager.Get), so an exception for the frozen lock in the one config would hide the same advisory in every lock of the inventory. Custom readers of each npm lock format, written first to bound such an exception, were refuted one YAML feature at a time (independent_review); the scanner's own scoping replaces them.
